rationale:
The Governance Board finds that the POST-700 governance framework is HARDENED at the documentation-and-standards layer. The HARDENING charter's primary objective — 'Prevent Recurrence — Not Correct Symptoms' — has been achieved at the governance design level. All 8 root cause failure classes documented by Agent K (FC-001 through FC-010) have corresponding prohibitions in the Scan Methodology Standard (FM-001 through FM-008), field extraction rules in the Governance Detection Standard (Section 3 mandatory prohibitions), or ownership safeguards in the Portfolio Stewardship Framework (Principle 2 acceptance requirement, Principle 3 closure disposition).

The Board draws a critical distinction between HARDENED (the governance framework, rules, standards, and prohibitions are published, binding, and sufficient to prevent recurrence if followed) and FULLY OPERATIONAL (every enforcement mechanism in the codebase has been upgraded to comply with the new standards). This session's charter was HARDENING, not COMPLETION. The deliverables — 6 standards, 8 forbidden-methodology prohibitions, 5 stewardship principles, transfer-accept-approve-close workflow, maintenance cadences, escalation paths — constitute a hardened governance framework.

However, the Board acknowledges two enforcement gaps identified by Agent U's simulation (Scenario A: governance guard forward-scan; Scenario C: no automated series closure gate) and 4 additional operational gaps (Agent I: 3 non-compliant tools; Agent N: 0/6 ownership acceptances; Agent C: 24 phantom references; Agent J: 4 P0 knowledge base updates). These gaps do not prevent the framework from being HARDENED — the rules exist and are binding — but they MUST be closed before the framework can be declared FULLY OPERATIONAL. The governance guard upgrade is the single highest-priority action because it bridges the gap between documented standards and runtime enforcement.

Precedent: This decision mirrors the 700-series MAINTENANCE MODE declaration at S723 — a framework was established and declared active, with operational upgrades (governance guard DL-029 fix, CURRENT_BASELINES §3 refresh) deferred to subsequent sessions. The maintenance framework operated successfully for 4+ sessions before S724 identified the ownership gaps that S725 is now closing.

The Board declares: THE FRAMEWORK IS HARDENED. The rules are published. The prohibitions are binding. The ownership is assigned. Now execute the operational upgrades.
